external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser accessing the web application.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application serving browser requests and placing jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: A background worker that picks up jobs and performs the heavy work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue holding jobs placed by the web application and picked up by the background worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker and used to keep application log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: The configuration store for the web application, including its queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: The configuration store for the worker, including its database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: access application
data_flows.description: The user's browser accesses the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: enqueue jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_flows.name: pick up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up

data_flows.name: read-write database
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.

data_flows.name: read configuration
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from its configuration store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: read configuration
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from its configuration store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: … the worker has a worker config

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet outside the organisation's network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The web tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend tier containing the queue, worker and database behind the web tier.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is reachable from the internet because a user's browser talks to it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source says the browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface because it is described as a background worker process rather than a web-serving application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as a background worker that picks up jobs and does work.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is confidential because it holds the web application's queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application config holds queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is confidential because it holds the worker's database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker config holds database credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The message queue holds business-critical data because it holds application jobs.
assumptions.basis: The source states that jobs are put onto the message queue; jobs are operating records under the controlled asset vocabulary.

assumptions.assumption: The database holds business-critical data because it holds application log records.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database holds the application's log records.

assumptions.assumption: The web application handles business-critical data because it places application jobs onto the queue.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application puts jobs onto the message queue.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker handles business-critical data because it picks up jobs and does the work.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the background worker picks up jobs and does the work.

assumptions.assumption: The public internet, web tier and backend tier are separate network trust boundaries because the source distinguishes those network locations.
assumptions.basis: The source places the browser across the public internet and outside the organisation's network.

assumptions.assumption: The web tier is a network trust boundary because the source identifies it as the location where the web application runs.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies a distinct web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The backend tier is a network trust boundary because the source identifies it as a separate tier behind the web tier.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies a distinct backend tier behind the web tier.
